A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRGen work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematical-reasoning evaluations, latency measurements, hyperparameter ablations, token analyses, and generation case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds general-reasoning, code-generation, and comparative accuracy and efficiency results.

M1.justification: The core dynamic trigger, corrective vector, hybrid loss, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. However, v1 Appendix B.2's optional online adaptive-lambda procedure is omitted in v2, removing an explicitly described procedural variant. This does not establish a change to the algorithm used in the main experiments.

E1.justification: V2 adds actual evaluations on GPQA for general reasoning and EvalPlus for code generation, substantially extending the mathematical-task coverage. AIME2024/2025, HMMT2025, AMC, and MATH500 remain; MATH500 was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: V1 Table 2 compares the base models with SRGen and explicitly excludes head-to-head post-hoc reflection comparisons in Appendix D. V2 adds Self-Refine to Table 2 and evaluates MI-Peak and SLOT in the accuracy and efficiency comparisons of Tables 3–4. SLOT already appeared in v1's combination experiment, but its additional comparisons are new.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the full-AIME2024 latency-versus-iterations experiment with MATH500 workload scaling and a 100-problem comparison reporting runtime, tokens, and peak memory. V2 also adds greedy comparisons involving Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. The principal sampling temperature, top-p, generation limits, and five-run accuracy aggregation remain unchanged; the runtime results therefore do not demonstrate a same-setting speedup across versions.

E4.justification: V2 extends the voting analysis from AMC to AMC and MATH500, and replaces the single aggregated critical-token analysis with distributions for two models on MATH500 and GPQA. The old latency/activation sweep disappears, and the lambda-sensitivity plot changes. Most hyperparameter analyses, loss-dynamics plots, and both case studies are retained, with substantial relocation.

E5.justification: Five-run accuracy averaging remains, but v2 removes v1's reproducibility statement mentioning fixed random seeds in the companion artifact. This reduces seed documentation without establishing fewer runs or changed seed use. Neither version supplies confidence intervals or significance tests for the main accuracy results.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial benchmark, comparator, and resource-cost results and removes v1 Table 2's detailed Cons@5 and Pass@5 results. Matched five-run accuracy entries also change: Distill-Qwen-7B on HMMT2025 changes from 18.0 to 19.3, and Distill-Llama-8B on AIME2025 from 32.7 to 36.0. Voting and lambda-ablation curves are revised, while the SLOT-combination results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, its assumptions and proof, the Lagrangian correspondence, and the joint-descent lemma are retained after Appendix B.1 becomes C.1. A localized mathematical correction appears in Appendix I: the displayed sine-power derivation replaces an inappropriately invoked cosine-sum identity with the sine-difference identity actually needed.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains proactive token-level self-reflection through transient hidden-state correction. V2 adds an explicit contribution claim about gains over strong baselines with lower latency overhead and broadens the conclusion to general reasoning and code generation. It removes the abstract's specific Cons@5 improvement and replaces the conclusion's approximately 50% overhead claim with qualitative wording.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning hidden-state and gradient access, imperfect critical-position selection, and model/task-dependent hyperparameter tuning. These qualify the retained plug-and-play applicability claims. The principal interpretations of critical tokens, contextual fidelity, self-consistency, and exploration remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds GPQA and EvalPlus prompts. Conversely, v2 removes v1 Appendix B.2's practical optimization, stopping, numerical-stability, and diagnostic guidance, together with the dedicated reproducibility statement. Core hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain, and the same code URL is retained as a footnote; no changed repository availability is established.

R1.justification: V2 adds the GPQA and EvalPlus references, Rein et al. and Liu et al., while retaining the related-work taxonomy and most citations. Removing the baseline-exclusion discussion and adding direct comparisons shifts some positioning toward empirical competitiveness, but the claimed distinction from post-hoc refinement and sample-level optimization remains.

P1.justification: The introduction gains an explicit contribution list, experimental discussion is extensively rewritten, hyperparameter ablations move to Appendix G, and critical-token analysis moves into Section 5.6. Practical guidance, baseline-scope discussion, and the reproducibility statement disappear, while limitations are added and ethics text is rewritten. V2 also contains an empty 'More Results' appendix heading and an unfinished sentence in Section 5.5.

P2.justification: V2 switches to two columns, restructures Tables 1–2, adds comparison Tables 3–4, and substantially revises the efficiency, voting, critical-token, and ablation displays. Retained figures and case studies are resized and relocated. Figure 1's three loss-equation boxes become blank in v2, although the corresponding equations remain in the main text.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's explicit avoidance of direct reflection-baseline comparisons by adding Self-Refine, MI-Peak, and broader SLOT comparisons with measured resource costs. GPQA/EvalPlus evaluations and concrete deployment limitations also strengthen the evidence for applicability. Removing the detailed Cons@5/Pass@5 results and practical guidance, plus unfinished text and blank diagram labels, are drawbacks. Nevertheless, the new comparisons resolve an important evidential gap and provide a substantially stronger basis for assessing SRGen's advantages and tradeoffs.
